What is Pico Laser (PICO WAY)?

PicoLaser (PicoWay) is a medical skin laser manufactured by American company Syneron Candela.
Compared to conventional Q-switched lasers, the irradiation time is shorter, reducing damage to the skin while providing more effective results.
It can irradiate lasers with three different wavelengths (1,064nm, 785nm, 532nm), so it can respond to various skin problems and concerns. Adjustments can be made to suit the condition of the skin, the extent of age spots, freckles, and melasma, and their color tone, allowing for efficient irradiation.
The Pico Laser is a highly safe laser that has received pharmaceutical approval from the Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare and approval from the FDA (U.S. Food and Drug Administration).

Recommended for people like this

  • Those who are concerned about age spots, freckles, and melasma
  • Those who are concerned about acne scars
  • People who are worried about dull skin
  • Those who want to have fair skin
  • People who are worried about fine lines
  • Those who are concerned about pigmentation
  • Those who want to regain their skin firmness
  • Those who want tattoo removal

Symptoms and areas targeted for treatment

Stains, freckles, dullness

When irradiating spots, freckles, or dull skin, a scab will form after the treatment and then fall off.
Effective against age spots, freckles, and dullness of various sizes, numbers, shapes, and colors.

melasma

For melasma, choose low-power irradiation. Shock waves can break down even the smallest melanin pigments, which is difficult to do with conventional lasers.

Wrinkles, acne scars, enlarged pores

Laser shock waves create small cavities within the epidermis rather than on the epidermis, promoting collagen growth and skin cell regeneration, improving wrinkles, acne scars, and enlarged pores.
Compared to traditional lasers, there is less damage to the epidermis, which means less pain.

Advantages of pico laser

Expected to be more effective than conventional laser treatment

It is also effective for treating light-colored spots and dullness that are difficult to treat with conventional laser treatment.

Few side effects

This treatment uses shock waves rather than heat to break down the pigment. Therefore, there is less damage to the skin and side effects are less likely to occur.

Treatment can be performed in a short time

Since it can oscillate in units of one trillionth of a second, the treatment time is short at 10 to 15 minutes.

Pico laser side effects and downtime

Side effects/risks

  • In rare cases, you may experience some redness after treatment, but it usually subsides within a few days.
  • In rare cases, blisters or internal bleeding may occur after treatment, but this usually subsides within two weeks.

Downtime and precautions

Treatment time: about 10-15 minutes
Downtime: Almost none *There are individual differences

  • If blisters or internal bleeding occur, there will be downtime of 1 to 2 weeks.
  • If post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation occurs, there may be downtime of several weeks to several months. (*Extremely rare.)
